items.headline: Top online savings rates held at 4.00% this week.
items.summary: Three of the twenty accounts we track nudged up by 0.05 points and none cut. If your account is under 3.75%, today is a good morning to compare.

items.headline: The rotating 5% category switches to grocery stores through September 30.
items.summary: Activate it once and the cap covers about $1,500 of spend. A reminder lands on your Today view on the last morning.

items.headline: A stackable 20% code on winter tires ends Friday.
items.summary: It works with the retailer's rebate on the same order, which brings a $600 set to about $430 after both.

items.headline: October playbook: buy patio furniture and jeans now, wait on TVs and toys.
items.summary: Clearance cycles favour outdoor goods and denim this month; big electronics drop again in late November.

items.headline: The 50/30/20 tune up: a ten minute look at your paycheck split.
items.summary: Three questions to ask before the next pay run, with a worksheet you can fill in on the Goals tab.

items.headline: A second tracked account moved up 0.05 this week, and none has cut.
items.summary: Bank H (illustrative), further down the tracked list, is 3.65% this morning; the top tracked rate stays 4.00%.

items.headline: Activation for the October categories opened on one of the two tracked cards.
items.summary: Turning it on today costs nothing and the 5% starts October 1; the grocery category keeps paying through September 30.

items.headline: A 15% code on running shoes stacks with a $20 rebate through Sunday.
items.summary: On a $140 pair the two together bring the price to about $99.

items.headline: Denim clearance spread to three of the four chains we track, at 40% off.
items.summary: A $90 pair is about $54 this week; the fourth chain's published prices had not moved by six.

items.headline: October holds three paydays if your alternate Friday paycheck lands on October 2.
items.summary: The third paycheck has no bills assigned to it, and the split worksheet shows where it could go before it arrives.

items.headline: The top tracked rate holds at 4.00% into the Fed's meeting week.
items.summary: All twenty tracked accounts and CDs are unchanged since Friday; Bank A (illustrative) still leads at 4.00%.

items.headline: The grocery category runs sixteen more days, and unused cap doesn't carry.
items.summary: Spend under the $1,500 cap counts through September 30; whatever is left of it that night is gone.

items.headline: A 25% code on kids' winter coats runs through Thursday night.
items.summary: It applies to sale items as well; an $80 coat comes to about $60 with it.

items.headline: TVs sit near August prices; their cut comes in late November.
items.summary: The tracked 65 inch sets sit within $30 of August prices; the deep cuts follow Thanksgiving.

items.headline: The 50/30/20 split starts with net pay, not the offer letter.
items.summary: Take one pay stub, find the deposit amount and split that; the taxes already left.

items.headline: A tracked savings account moved up 0.05 to 3.90% before the Fed.
items.summary: Bank B (illustrative) repriced overnight, the first tracked move of the Fed's week.

items.headline: October to December categories published: warehouse clubs, and online retail.
items.summary: Both tracked rotating cards named their fourth quarter categories; activation windows open before October 1.

items.headline: Two grocery delivery codes stack this week: $15 off and free delivery.
items.summary: On a $120 order the pair brings it to about $105 with no delivery fee.

items.headline: Outdoor furniture clearance began at two of the three tracked home retailers.
items.summary: An $899 four piece set is listed at $599 this morning; the third retailer had not moved.

items.headline: The date sets the deposit: $4,000 in a year, $154 a payday.
items.summary: Divide what's left of a goal by the alternate Friday paydays before its date, then round up.

items.headline: Fed decision at 2 PM today; no tracked account moved overnight.
items.summary: No tracked account moved overnight; the average of the twenty sits at 3.54%.

items.headline: Activating next quarter early costs nothing where the card allows it.
items.summary: One tracked card opens activation on September 23, the other on October 1; both run through December 31.

items.headline: At the tire retailer, 10% off beats $20 off past $200.
items.summary: Two codes, one order; on $500 the percentage code wins by $30.

items.headline: Halloween costumes hold their price through October; the candy doesn't.
items.summary: Costumes are full price until the week of the 31st; candy is cut in the last three days.

items.headline: Fixed costs first: what share of net pay is already spoken for?
items.summary: Add rent, insurance, minimum payments and utilities, then divide by net pay; past 60% the 20% has no room.

items.headline: The Fed raised a quarter point; a tracked CD moved 0.10 overnight.
items.summary: Bank D (illustrative) is 3.75% on its one year CD this morning; the twenty savings accounts held.

items.headline: Past the $1,500 cap the grocery category pays 1%, not 5%.
items.summary: Beyond the cap a flat 3% grocery card wins; the cap line is in the card's app.

items.headline: The 25% coats code ends tonight, and no rebate stacks with it.
items.summary: Orders placed by 11:59 PM ET keep the code; the rebate form is separate and doesn't combine.

items.headline: The third tracked home retailer joined the patio clearance at 35% off.
items.summary: All three now list the same four piece set between $549 and $599.

items.headline: Where the 20% sits matters: 0.37% against 4.00% on $200 a payday.
items.summary: Over a year of alternate Friday deposits the difference is about $100 in interest.

items.headline: A money market up 0.10, a savings account down 0.05, overnight.
items.summary: Bank C (illustrative) is 3.80%; Bank E cut to 3.70%, the week's only cut since the Fed's move.

items.headline: The grocery category has twelve days left: how much cap remains?
items.summary: The card's app shows spend toward the $1,500 cap; anything left after September 30 is gone.

items.headline: A 20% winter tire code opened today and runs through next Friday.
items.summary: Eight days to use it; the rebate form on the same order is separate and still applies.

items.headline: Grills joined the clearance: a $399 gas grill is listed at $279.
items.summary: The outdoor aisle is being emptied for holiday stock, and the grills go with the patio sets.

items.headline: The deposit that's automatic on payday is the one that happens.
items.summary: A standing transfer set for the morning after payday removes the decision; the amount can be $25.
